source.original_text: For the same hidden rotation, either exact precision-matvec reply reconstructs its counterpart at the same query point. \begin{aligned}Q_\kappa(x)&=(\kappa-1)Q_2(x)-(\kappa-2)x,\\Q_2(x)&=\frac{Q_\kappa(x)+(\kappa-2)x}{\kappa-1}.\end{aligned} \(d\in\mathbb N,\ d\ge2,\ \kappa\in\mathbb R,\ \kappa\ge2\). Both endpoints are included. Fix one arbitrary actual \(O\in O(d)\); both precision matrices use this same rotation, which remains the hidden input. For source indices \(i=1,\ldots,d\), define \(\theta_i=(i-\tfrac12)\pi/d\), \(\lambda_i(\eta)=(\eta+1)/2+(\eta-1)\cos\theta_i/2\), and the actual matrices \(A_\eta=O\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1(\eta),\ldots,\lambda_d(\eta))O^\top\). Lean uses zero-based indices, so its angle is \((i.\mathrm{val}+\tfrac12)\pi/d\). The local formula is total in \(\eta\); the assertions use only source-valid \(\eta=\kappa\) and \(\eta=2\). The actual reply is \(Q_\eta(x)=A_\eta x\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R^d\). The subscript 2 is the reference condition number, rather than a number of calls, a transpose query or a covariance inverse. The scalar \(\kappa-1\) is at least one and hence nonzero; this is derived internally from the source parameter range. Orthogonality, the scalar/diagonal/matrix affine identities and both actual reply formulas are not additional premises. The source experiment draws a Haar rotation independently of private randomness. The selected identity holds pointwise for every realization; this declaration does not assert a joint law, adaptive simulation, query cap, precision/cost comparison, Gaussian-target transport, or a separate formal spectral/positive-definite/normalizer theorem. The full fixed-spectrum lower bound retains its own fixed \(\delta\in(0,1)\), sufficiently large \(d\), \(2\le\kappa\le d^{1-\delta}\) and \(0<\varepsilon\le1/10\) conditions.

    let θ : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => ((i.val : ℝ) + 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (d : ℝ)
    let A : ℝ → Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ := fun η =>
      (O : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) *
        Matrix.diagonal (fun i => (η + 1) / 2 + (η - 1) / 2 * Real.cos (θ i)) *
        (O : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ).transpose
    let query : ℝ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) :=
      fun η x => WithLp.toLp 2 (A η *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp x)
    ∀ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d),
      query κ x = (κ - 1) • query 2 x - (κ - 2) • x ∧
      query 2 x = (κ - 1)⁻¹ • (query κ x + (κ - 2) • x)

blind_reconstruction.text:
For every natural number d with d ≥ 2, every real number κ with κ ≥ 2, and every real orthogonal d × d matrix O (with either determinant sign), index coordinates by i ∈ Fin d, that is, integers i = 0, …, d − 1. Define
θᵢ = (i + 1/2)π/d.
For each real parameter η, define
A(η) = O diagᵢ((η + 1)/2 + ((η − 1)/2) cos θᵢ) Oᵀ,
and define Qη : ℝᵈ → ℝᵈ by Qη(x) = A(η)x, using ordinary matrix-vector multiplication and the usual Euclidean coordinate identification.
Then every x ∈ ℝᵈ satisfies both vector identities
Qκ(x) = (κ − 1) Q₂(x) − (κ − 2)x,
and
Q₂(x) = (κ − 1)⁻¹ (Qκ(x) + (κ − 2)x).
Here scalar-vector products and vector sums and differences have their usual real meanings. The same d, κ, O, and x occur in both identities. Since κ ≥ 2, κ − 1 is nonzero and its displayed reciprocal is the usual real inverse. No probability law on O is specified.

import Mathlib.Data.Matrix.Diagonal
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.PiL2
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.Basic
import Mathlib.Tactic.FieldSimp
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring
import Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith
import Mathlib.Tactic.NormNum
open Matrix
/-!
# Actual same-rotation fixed-spectrum precision replies

Zhou--Suzuki arXiv:2610.20492v1, Section4.1 Equation11 and Remark4.2.
The two precision matrices use the literal cosine grid and the SAME hidden
orthogonal rotation. One exact precision-matvec reply reconstructs the other
at the same actual point in either direction. The number2 here is the
reference condition number, not a call count or inverse-covariance oracle.
All scalar/diagonal/orthogonal/conjugation/matvec and nonzero-reciprocal bridges
are proved internally. No supplied affine identity or reply-correctness premise.
Gaussian target/covariance/TV transport, operational adaptive/cost/precision
adapters, spectral/PosDef/normalizer background and both main lower bounds
remain separate.
-/

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.FixedSpectrumAffine
set_option autoImplicit false
theorem actual_affine_precision_query {d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d)
    {κ : ℝ} (hκ : 2 ≤ κ)
    (O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin d) ℝ) :
    let θ : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => ((i.val : ℝ) + 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (d : ℝ)
    let A : ℝ → Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ := fun η =>
      (O : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) *
        Matrix.diagonal (fun i => (η + 1) / 2 + (η - 1) / 2 * Real.cos (θ i)) *
        (O : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ).transpose
    let query : ℝ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) :=
      fun η x => WithLp.toLp 2 (A η *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp x)
    ∀ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d),
      query κ x = (κ - 1) • query 2 x - (κ - 2) • x ∧
      query 2 x = (κ - 1)⁻¹ • (query κ x + (κ - 2) • x) := by
  classical
  dsimp only
  let θ : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => ((i.val : ℝ) + 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (d : ℝ)
  let A : ℝ → Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ := fun η =>
    (O : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) *
      Matrix.diagonal (fun i => (η + 1) / 2 + (η - 1) / 2 * Real.cos (θ i)) *
      (O : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ).transpose
  let query : ℝ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) :=
    fun η x => WithLp.toLp 2 (A η *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp x)
  -- Align the zero-based indices with the literal one-based source grid.
  have hdpos : (0 : ℝ) < (d : ℝ) := by
    exact_mod_cast (lt_of_lt_of_le (by decide : (0 : ℕ) < 2) hd)
  have hd0 : (d : ℝ) ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt hdpos
  have hindex (i : Fin d) : θ i =
      (((i.val : ℝ) + 1 - 1 / 2) * Real.pi) / (d : ℝ) := by
    dsimp only [θ]
    field_simp [hd0]; ring
  -- Lift the actual entrywise identity through the diagonal and same O.
  have hscalar (i : Fin d) :
      (κ + 1) / 2 + (κ - 1) / 2 * Real.cos (θ i) =
      (κ - 1) * ((2 + 1) / 2 + (2 - 1) / 2 * Real.cos (θ i)) - (κ - 2) := by
    simp only [hindex i]
    ring
  have hdiag :
      Matrix.diagonal (fun i => (κ + 1) / 2 + (κ - 1) / 2 * Real.cos (θ i)) =
      (κ - 1) • Matrix.diagonal (fun i => (2 + 1) / 2 + (2 - 1) / 2 * Real.cos (θ i)) -
        (κ - 2) • (1 : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) := by
    ext i j
    by_cases hij : i = j
    · subst j
      simpa [Matrix.diagonal_apply, Matrix.one_apply] using hscalar i
    · simp [hij]
  -- Full orthogonal membership supplies the actual right identity.
  have hO : (O : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) *
      (O : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ).transpose = 1 :=
    (Matrix.mem_orthogonalGroup_iff (n := Fin d) (R := ℝ)).mp O.property
  have hmatrix : A κ = (κ - 1) • A 2 - (κ - 2) • 1 := by
    dsimp only [A]
    rw [hdiag, Matrix.mul_sub, Matrix.sub_mul]
    simp only [Matrix.mul_smul, Matrix.smul_mul, Matrix.mul_one, hO]
  -- Reverse conversion uses a genuinely nonzero known scalar.
  have hnz : κ - 1 ≠ 0 := by linarith
  intro x
  have hforward : query κ x = (κ - 1) • query 2 x - (κ - 2) • x := by
    apply WithLp.ofLp_injective 2
    change A κ *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp x =
      (κ - 1) • (A 2 *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp x) - (κ - 2) • WithLp.ofLp x
    rw [hmatrix]
    simp only [Matrix.sub_mulVec, Matrix.smul_mulVec, Matrix.one_mulVec]
  refine ⟨hforward, ?_⟩
  change query 2 x = (κ - 1)⁻¹ • (query κ x + (κ - 2) • x)
  rw [hforward, sub_add_cancel, smul_smul, inv_mul_cancel₀ hnz, one_smul]
end AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.FixedSpectrumAffine

notation.text: Actual precision reply at scalar parameter η; both κ and 2 use the same hidden rotation and deterministic angle grid.

steps.title: Align the actual cosine grid
steps.text: The zero-based coordinate i.val corresponds to source coordinate i.val+1. Derive positivity of d from the source dimension bound, then identify the two exact angle expressions. All matrices retain the same angle grid.
steps.lean: hdpos/hd0 derive a genuine nonzero denominator; hindex proves the exact source-index alignment.

steps.title: Lift the scalar affine identity to the diagonal
steps.text: Expand the literal eigenvalue formula at κ and at 2. The entrywise affine equality lifts to the diagonal matrix by comparing equal and distinct indices; no arbitrary scalar sequence or hypothesized matrix equality is introduced.
steps.lean: hscalar uses hindex and real polynomial arithmetic; hdiag proves the actual diagonal identity entrywise.

steps.title: Conjugate through the same hidden rotation
steps.text: Full orthogonal-group membership supplies OOᵀ=I. Distribute the actual matrix product and commute the known scalars through it. This yields the actual source precision identity with the same rotation on both sides.
steps.lean: hO applies the actual mem_orthogonalGroup_iff with explicit Fin d/real parameters. hmatrix consumes hdiag, matrix distribution, scalar multiplication and hO.

steps.title: Recover each actual reply
steps.text: Apply that matrix equality to the actual queried vector and transport its entries through the Euclidean representation. The forward formula gives a reply at κ from the reply at 2. Rearrange it and multiply by the genuinely nonzero inverse κ−1 for the reverse formula.
steps.lean: hforward uses WithLp.ofLp_injective, sub_mulVec/smul_mulVec/one_mulVec. hnz follows from hκ. The final inverse cancellation proves the reverse equality, with no totalized-zero shortcut.

steps.title: Compare two actual hidden inputs
steps.text: Instantiate the producer for O₁ and O₂ at the same x. Equal actual κ replies give equal actual reference-2 replies by the reverse maps; the forward maps give the converse. This is a genuine same-point observational consumer, separate from Gaussian target or algorithm-law transport.
steps.lean: Tests.GaussianComplexityFixedSpectrumAffine calls the producer twice and applies congrArg to each known scalar/vector reply map.
